# Investigate a Server Saturated by Logging

[← Together AI](../README.md) · [Every Together AI question](../../together-ai.md) · [Read it on TrueInterview](https://trueinterview.io/study/investigate-a-server-saturated-by-logging)

---

A server is under heavy load and logs might be part of the picture. Walk through how you would isolate the cause, get the service back to a healthy state, and stop the issue from happening again.

### Constraints & Assumptions
The prompt mentions log tracing and a saturated server but doesn't say whether the bottleneck is CPU, memory, disk space, storage throughput, or a logging sink. Pin that down before you adjust any logging behavior.

### Clarifying Questions
Which resource is maxed out? Has the volume of logs changed recently? Are producers waiting on a sink, or is an unbounded queue growing without limit? Which logs do you actually need for debugging or compliance?

### What a Strong Answer Covers
Resource identification, a safe short-term fix, bounded logging, retention and rotation, and proof that the root cause was addressed.

### Follow-up Questions
If you delete a log file that a process still has open, does the space become available right away? What occurs when a remote log sink starts lagging? How would you cut down repetitive noise without burying the incident itself?

Overview:
Trace log-driven server saturation by working through resource attribution, producer and sink dynamics, bounded queues, rotation and retention, and verified remediation.
